summary: On node1, created the dedicated system account inventorysvc, installed and enabled a systemd unit (inventory-worker.service) running /usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker as that user, verified it was active/enabled, then performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured a healthy baseline (boot_id + running service under inventorysvc), issued systemctl reboot, confirmed the node became unreachable and later reachable again with a changed boot_id, and verified inventory-worker was active, enabled, and running as inventorysvc post-restart (systemd's WantedBy=multi-user.target auto-started it, no manual intervention needed).
actions_performed: Inspected /usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker and confirmed init system is systemd 229
Created system user 'inventorysvc' via sudo useradd --system --no-create-home --shell /usr/sbin/nologin
Ran systemctl daemon-reload and systemctl enable --now inventory-worker
Verified service active/enabled and main process running as inventorysvc
Captured pre-restart boot_id baseline and confirmed service health
Issued 'sudo systemctl reboot' on node1 in background so acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Confirmed node1 briefly unreachable (connection refused), then polled until reachable again
Confirmed boot_id changed (8336c3a1... -> 39510b7f...) proving an actual restart occurred
Verified inventory-worker.service is active, enabled, and running under inventorysvc post-restart

evidence.requirement: os-comparison-worker installed as managed service 'inventory-worker' under dedicated 'inventorysvc' account
evidence.summary: Confirmed binary exists, created inventorysvc system user, wrote systemd unit with User=inventorysvc, enabled+started the service, and verified via ps that the running process (PID 2920) is owned by inventorysvc.
Captured pre-restart boot_id (8336c3a1-91fc-4135-b26a-5d2863cb2594) as the stable boot marker, with prior command confirming service was active.
Issued 'sudo systemctl reboot' backgrounded so the exec call returned an acknowledgement before disconnect; subsequent command showed connection refused, proving the node went down.

evidence.requirement: node1 changed boot identity proving actual restart
evidence.summary: Polled until node1 became reachable again; boot_id read as 39510b7f-5faf-498a-a522-628f41f3f943, differing from the pre-restart value, and uptime -s showed a new boot time (09:15:00 vs 09:14:07).

After restart, inventory-worker.service reported active/enabled and the running process (new PID 837) was confirmed via ps to be owned by inventorysvc, showing the service auto-started under the correct account after reboot.
